accepted.s: Which Governor-General was associated with the Anti-Infanticide Regulation of 1802?
accepted.x: The Anti-Infanticide Regulation was issued in 1802 during the tenure of Marquess Wellesley and prohibited infanticide.
accepted.tq: Match the social-reform measure with the correct Governor-General.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Anti-Human Sacrifice Act of 1845 was associated with:
accepted.x: The Anti-Human Sacrifice Act was enacted in 1845 during the tenure of Lord Hardinge I.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely placed reform Acts by their Governor-General.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sati Regulation of 1829:
1. It was associated with William Bentinck.
2. It made sati illegal.
3. Sati was treated as culpable homicide under the Regulation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Regulation XVII of 1829, associated with William Bentinck, prohibited sati and treated participation in it as culpable homicide.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the Act’s year, authority and legal consequence.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Age of Consent Act, 1891 — Lord Irwin
accepted.x: The Female Infanticide Act of 1870 was associated with Lord Mayo. Lansdowne was associated with the Age of Consent Act, Irwin with the Sarda Act, and the 1872 Native Marriage Act had no Governor-General specified in the table.
accepted.tq: Eliminate swapped Governor-General and Act combinations.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Native (Civil) Marriage Act of 1872, the minimum ages prescribed for girls and boys respectively were:
accepted.x: The Native or Brahmo Marriage Act of 1872 prescribed a minimum age of 14 years for girls and 18 years for boys.
accepted.tq: Read the age pair in the order asked and avoid reversing the two figures.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature associated with the Native (Brahmo/Civil) Marriage Act of 1872?
o: It prescribed 18 years as the minimum age for boys.
It fixed the age of consent for girls at 12 years.
It prescribed 14 years as the minimum age for girls.
accepted.x: The age of consent for girls being raised from 10 to 12 was a feature of the Age of Consent Act of 1891, not the Native Marriage Act of 1872. The 1872 Act also allowed inter-caste marriage and barred polygamy.
accepted.tq: Separate the age provisions of the 1872 and 1891 Acts.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Native (Civil) Marriage Act of 1872 was chiefly associated with the campaign of:
accepted.x: The Native or Brahmo Marriage Act of 1872 was a product of Keshab Chandra Sen’s campaign. It also barred polygamy and permitted inter-caste marriage.
accepted.tq: Match the reform legislation with the reformer who campaigned for it.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Age of Consent Act of 1891 raised the age of consent for girls from:
accepted.x: The Age of Consent Act of 1891 raised the age of consent for girls from 10 to 12 years.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact before-and-after numerical change.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who advocated the enactment of the Age of Consent Act of 1891?
accepted.x: Behramji Malabari, a Parsi reformer from Bombay, advocated the Age of Consent law. The Act was enacted during Lord Lansdowne’s tenure.
accepted.tq: Use the reformer–Act association rather than the Governor-General association.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Child Marriage Restraint Act, popularly known as the Sarda Act, was passed in:
accepted.x: The Child Marriage Restraint Act, or Sarda Act, was passed in 1929. It came into force on 1 April 1930.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of passage from the year in which the Act came into force.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the position regarding the Sarda Act?
o: It was moved by Har Bilas Sarda and came into force on 1 April 1930.
It was moved by Behramji Malabari and came into force on 1 April 1931.
It was moved by Keshab Chandra Sen and came into force in 1929.
It was moved by Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar and came into force in 1928.
accepted.x: Har Bilas Sarda moved the Act, which was passed in 1929 and came into force on 1 April 1930.
accepted.tq: Combine the mover, passage year and commencement date without confusing them.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Sarda Act was amended in:
accepted.x: The Child Marriage Restraint Act was amended in 1978.
accepted.tq: Identify the amendment year separately from the original enactment year.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following enactments in chronological order:
A. Age of Consent Act
B. Caste Disabilities Removal Act
C. Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act
D. Child Marriage Restraint Act
accepted.x: The correct sequence is the Caste Disabilities Removal Act of 1850, Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act of 1856, Age of Consent Act of 1891, and Child Marriage Restraint Act of 1929.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest 1850 Act and the latest 1929 Act.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the Caste Disabilities Removal Act of 1850 is correct?
1. It is also known as the Lex Loci Act.
2. It protected the inheritance rights of a person who converted to Christianity.
3. It dealt primarily with the abolition of sati.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Lex Loci Act protected the right of a convert to inherit ancestral property; abolition of sati was dealt with by the 1829 Sati Regulation.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that assigns the subject of one reform Act to another.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Why did orthodox Hindus regard the Lex Loci Act of 1850 as a possible incentive to conversion?
o: It permitted converts to hold high military offices automatically.
It abolished all caste distinctions by executive order.
It granted converts exemption from all colonial taxes.
It allowed converts to retain the right to inherit ancestral property.
accepted.x: The Act allowed a person who converted, including a convert to Christianity, to retain the right to inherit ancestral property. This was viewed by orthodox Hindus as an incentive to conversion and became one of the grievances associated with 1857.
accepted.tq: Apply the legal provision to the social reaction it produced.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement most accurately describes the legislative history of the Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act of 1856?
o: It was drafted under Mayo and enacted in 1872 under Irwin.
It was drafted under Bentinck and enacted in 1856 under Lansdowne.
It was drafted under Dalhousie and enacted in July 1856 under Canning.
It was drafted under Canning and enacted in 1850 under Dalhousie.
accepted.x: The bill was prepared during Dalhousie’s tenure but the Act was enacted in July 1856 under Lord Canning. The Act legalised widow remarriage and legitimised the children of such marriages.
accepted.tq: Resolve the close Governor-General distinction by separating drafting from enactment.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Institution)
a. Deva Samaj
b. Seva Samiti
c. Social Service League
d. Sharada Sadan

List-II (Founder)
i. Pandita Ramabai
ii. N.M. Joshi
iii. Shiv Narayan Agnihotri
iv. Hriday Nath Kunzru

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Deva Samaj was founded by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri, Seva Samiti by Hriday Nath Kunzru, Social Service League by N.M. Joshi, and Sharada Sadan by Pandita Ramabai.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure institution–founder pairs and eliminate the remaining codes.
accepted.sec: Reform institutions → founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who founded the Seva Sadan in Bombay?
o: Behramji M. Malabari, with Dayaram Gidumal
accepted.x: Seva Sadan was founded in Bombay by Behramji M. Malabari with Dayaram Gidumal. It worked for the education, medical assistance and welfare of exploited and abandoned women across castes.
accepted.tq: Separate Seva Sadan from the similarly named Poona Seva Sadan.
accepted.sec: Reform institutions → founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Poona Seva Sadan was founded by:
o: Shiv Narayan Agnihotri and Hriday Nath Kunzru
accepted.x: Poona Seva Sadan was founded by Ramabai Ranade and G.K. Devadhar in 1909.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between institutions with the common name ‘Seva Sadan’.
accepted.sec: Reform institutions → founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which institution was founded by Pandita Ramabai in Bombay in 1889 and later shifted to Poona?
accepted.x: Pandita Ramabai founded Sharada Sadan in Bombay in 1889; it was later shifted to Poona. Arya Mahila Samaj was founded by her in Poona in 1882.
accepted.tq: Use the institution’s place and year to distinguish it from another institution founded by the same reformer.
accepted.sec: Reform institutions → founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Pandita Ramabai:
1. She founded Arya Mahila Samaj in Poona.
2. Arya Mahila Samaj was founded in 1882.
3. She founded Sarada Niketan in Guntur in 1922.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Sarada Niketan in Guntur was founded by Unnava Lakshminarayana with his wife Lakshmibayamma.
accepted.tq: Catch the founder swap between institutions associated with women’s education.
accepted.sec: Reform institutions → founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Sarada Niketan, described as a women’s gurukulam, was established at Guntur in 1922 by:
accepted.x: Sarada Niketan was established at Guntur in 1922 by Unnava Lakshminarayana with his wife Lakshmibayamma.
accepted.tq: Test the Andhra-specific institution, place, year and founder together.
accepted.sec: Reform institutions → founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Deva Samaj was founded at Lahore in 1887 by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri, so the institution–place–year pairing itself is correct; however, among the listed institutional associations, it is the one that is not correctly matched if Deva Samaj is paired with Radhakant Deb. Radhakant Deb was associated with the orthodox Dharma Sabha, not Deva Samaj.
accepted.tq: Check the founder association rather than accepting a familiar place-and-year pairing.
accepted.sec: Reform institutions → founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Social Service League was founded in Bombay in 1911 by:
accepted.x: N.M. Joshi founded the Social Service League in Bombay in 1911.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with its founder using the distinctive place and year as confirmation.
accepted.sec: Reform institutions → founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the founder and year of Seva Samiti?
accepted.x: Seva Samiti was founded by Hriday Nath Kunzru at Allahabad in 1914.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the founders of the similarly named Seva institutions.
accepted.sec: Reform institutions → founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The present legal position regarding the minimum marriageable age under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 is:
o: 16 years for women and 18 years for men
18 years for women and 18 years for men
18 years for women and 21 years for men
21 years for women and 21 years for men
accepted.x: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 provides a minimum marriageable age of 18 years for women and 21 years for men. The proposal to raise women’s age to 21 had not become law as of January 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the law presently in force from a proposal that has not yet become law.
accepted.sec: Social-reform Acts → year, Governor-General, minimum ages  [APPSC]
